briefing.executive_summary:
The competitive landscape for Figma in 2025 is characterized by a diverse set of competitors, each with unique strengths and market positions. Adobe remains a dominant force in the creative software industry, leveraging its extensive suite of tools and strong brand presence. Despite its size, Adobe faces challenges from Figma's rapid growth and innovative collaboration features, which appeal to modern design teams. Atlassian, known for its project management and collaboration tools, offers a different kind of competition, focusing on enterprise solutions and deep integration with AI capabilities. This positions Atlassian as a strong contender in the collaboration market, particularly for large organizations.

Balsamiq and Banani represent niche competitors with distinct offerings. Balsamiq focuses on low-fidelity wireframing, catering to teams that prioritize speed and simplicity in the early stages of design. Its straightforward approach contrasts with Figma's high-fidelity capabilities. Banani, on the other hand, leverages AI to automate UI design processes, appealing to non-designers and teams looking for rapid prototyping solutions. This diverse competitive landscape highlights the varied needs of design teams and the importance of differentiation in features and pricing strategies.

competitors.name: Adobe

pricing.content: Adobe offers a range of pricing plans for its Creative Cloud services. The Creative Cloud Standard plan is priced at $54.99 per month with an annual contract billed monthly, while the Creative Cloud Pro plan costs $69.99 per month under the same terms. For students and teachers, Adobe provides a discounted rate of $19.99 per month for the first year, which increases to $39.99 per month upon renewal. Adobe also offers standalone products like Acrobat Pro for $19.99 per month.

sources.summary: Creative Cloud Standard is $54.99/month, Pro is $69.99/month; student rate $19.99/month first year, $39.99/month renewal.
Acrobat Pro costs $19.99/month with advanced PDF editing and e-signature tools.
Adobe Express Premium is $9.99/month, offering 250 generative AI credits and extensive templates.
Creative Cloud student discount is $15.99/month for the first year, then $39.99/month.
Photoshop can be purchased standalone or as part of a multi-app plan.

key_features.content: Adobe's key features include a comprehensive suite of creative tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, and Premiere Pro, which are part of the Creative Cloud. Adobe Express offers a vast library of customizable templates, AI-powered design tools, and mobile editing capabilities. Adobe Acrobat Pro provides advanced PDF editing, accessibility features, and e-signature solutions. The integration of Adobe Fonts and Stock enhances design capabilities, while collaboration and social media scheduling features are also available.

sources.summary: Adobe Express features include customizable templates, AI design tools, and mobile editing.
Acrobat features include text and image editing, PDF merging, and accessibility tools.
Acrobat Pro offers accessible PDF creation and compliance checks with an Action Wizard.
Acrobat includes AI insights for document tasks, interactive PDF Spaces, and e-signatures.
Guidance on completing pending feature installations in Adobe Acrobat.

market_positioning.content: Adobe is a market leader in digital media and marketing solutions, generating nearly $24 billion annually. It is known for its comprehensive suite of creative tools and its ability to generate more revenue per employee compared to competitors like Figma. Adobe's established business model and cash-rich operations make it a preferred choice for value investors, despite Figma's faster revenue growth. Adobe's focus on AI integration and its mature generative AI platform, Firefly, further solidify its market position.

sources.summary: Adobe generates nearly $24 billion annually, outpacing Figma's growth rate.
Adobe is a cash-rich incumbent with modest multiples, preferred by value investors.
Adobe generates $10 billion in annual free cash flow, trading at a P/E under 18.
Adobe's Creative Cloud is comprehensive, covering brand, print, and web design.
Adobe XD offers strong offline support and integration with other Adobe tools.

target_audience.content: Adobe targets a wide range of customers, including individual creatives, businesses, and educational institutions. Its products are used across various industries for content creation, marketing, and digital media management. Adobe Target, part of the Adobe Experience Cloud, is designed to personalize and enhance customer experiences across web, mobile, and social media channels. This makes Adobe's solutions suitable for e-commerce platforms, traditional banks, and other businesses seeking to optimize user engagement and conversion rates.

sources.summary: Adobe Target is used for content recommendations and experience targeting in various industries.
Adobe Target personalizes customer experiences across digital channels to maximize revenue.
Adobe Target offers extensive options for targeting information to customers based on behavior.
Adobe Target provides tools for personalization and testing, including Experience Targeting and A/B Testing.
HanesBrands uses Adobe Target for personalization, achieving a 41% lift in engagement.

recent_developments.content: In recent years, Adobe has focused on integrating AI into its product offerings, with AI-influenced annual recurring revenue now exceeding one-third of its business. In 2025, Adobe announced its acquisition of Semrush for $1.9 billion, expanding its capabilities in digital marketing. The company has also faced challenges, such as a significant drop in stock price due to AI disruption concerns, leading to a $25 billion stock buyback plan to stabilize its market value.

sources.summary: Adobe announced the acquisition of Semrush for $1.9 billion in November 2025.
Adobe is a global leader in digital media, with a market cap of $109.4 billion.
Adobe's AI-influenced ARR exceeds one-third of its business, with strong revenue growth.
Adobe's stock price fell significantly, prompting a $25 billion buyback to counter AI disruption.
Adobe's 2025 10-K report highlights significant financial growth and strategic AI integration.

key_threats: Adobe's Creative Cloud Pro plan at $69.99/month offers a comprehensive suite of tools that Figma cannot match in breadth, posing a challenge for users needing multiple creative applications.
Adobe's integration of AI across its product suite, including the mature Firefly platform, provides advanced capabilities that Figma's AI features may struggle to compete with.
The extensive library of Adobe Stock assets, with over 350 million photos and videos, offers a resource advantage that Figma lacks.
Adobe's established market presence and revenue generation capabilities make it a formidable competitor in terms of financial stability and investment potential.
Adobe's ability to offer significant discounts to students and educators at $19.99/month for the first year creates a strong entry point for future professional users.
opportunities: Adobe lacks a strong collaborative design feature like Figma's real-time editing, which Figma should leverage to attract teams needing seamless collaboration.
Adobe's pricing for individual apps like Photoshop at $19.99/month is higher than Figma's Professional plan at $15/month, which Figma can highlight to attract cost-conscious users.
Adobe's focus on a broad suite of tools may dilute its specialization in UI/UX design, allowing Figma to position itself as the expert in this niche.
Adobe's complex pricing structure and higher costs for comprehensive plans could be a deterrent for small teams, which Figma can exploit by offering simpler, more affordable pricing.
Adobe's generative AI features are not as integrated into the design workflow as Figma's, providing an opportunity for Figma to enhance its AI capabilities in context-specific applications.

competitors.name: Atlassian

pricing.content: Atlassian offers a range of pricing plans tailored to different team sizes and needs. Their Free plan supports up to 10 users with basic features, while the Standard plan costs approximately $8.15 per user per month when billed annually. For larger teams, the Enterprise plan starts at $155,000 per year for 801 users, offering advanced features like BYOK encryption and centralized administration. Discounts are available for community and academic customers, with up to 75% off for eligible users.

sources.summary: Enterprise plan starts at $155,000/year for 801 users, with advanced features like BYOK encryption and centralized administration.
Free plan available for up to 10 users with 2GB storage and community support.
Jira Software Standard plan costs $8.15/user/month annually, saving $1,920/year for 100 users.
Confluence Premium plan costs $10.44 per user per month, with features like unlimited storage and 24/7 support.
Cloud pricing offers 75% off for eligible community customers and 50% off for academic customers.

key_features.content: Atlassian's key features include advanced project management tools and AI-driven capabilities. Their products like Jira and Confluence offer features such as customizable workflows, intelligent search, and issue summarization to enhance productivity. Atlassian Intelligence integrates AI to assist with repetitive tasks, providing insights and reducing manual effort. Additionally, their products support integrations with other tools, offering a seamless workflow for teams.

sources.summary: Atlassian Intelligence offers features like issue summarization, content assistance, and intelligent search to improve project efficiency.
Confluence offers advanced admin controls, unlimited storage, and 24/7 support with a 99.9% uptime SLA.
Jira provides customizable workflows, out-of-the-box reports, and AI-driven insights for better decision-making.
New features include capacity planning, project budgeting, and custom reporting, integrated with AI capabilities.
Workforce Optimization in Jira Service Management includes features like agent availability and capacity limits.

market_positioning.content: Atlassian positions itself as a leader in the collaboration and project management space, with a strong focus on enterprise customers and AI integration. The company is recognized for its deep penetration in the enterprise market and its ability to drive digital transformation through AI-powered tools. Atlassian's products are designed to support remote and hybrid work environments, making them a preferred choice for organizations undergoing digital transformation.

sources.summary: Atlassian has greater upside potential with deeper enterprise penetration and stronger AI adoption compared to Figma.
Atlassian and Figma lead in R&D, with Atlassian focusing on tech and business collaborations.
Atlassian Marketplace highlights Figma's integration with Jira, showcasing collaboration between the two platforms.
Figma for Jira app in partnership with Atlassian, enhancing design context in Jira.
Atlassian focuses on human+AI design to enhance teamwork and eliminate busywork.

target_audience.content: Atlassian's target audience includes a wide range of industries such as consulting services, software development, and project management. Their products are used by over 260,000 organizations worldwide, including large enterprises and small teams. Atlassian's tools are designed to cater to both basic users and power users, providing a flexible platform that can scale with the needs of different organizations.

sources.summary: Atlassian's software is used by consulting services, software development tools, and project management companies.
Atlassian provides immediate technical support and agile resolution of complex problems for its customers.
Jira Service Management is used by over 60,000 customers, offering exceptional service experiences.
Atlassian is chosen by companies like Domino's and Delivery Hero for its intuitive and advanced platform.
90% of Atlassian's customers paying $50K+ annually use more than 3 Atlassian products, showcasing cross-selling success.

recent_developments.content: In recent years, Atlassian has made significant strides in AI and acquisitions to enhance its product offerings. In 2024, they launched Rovo, an AI teammate, and acquired Rewatch, a meeting bot company. In 2025, Atlassian acquired Cycle App Inc. and The Browser Company, expanding their capabilities in developer productivity and web browsing. These developments highlight Atlassian's commitment to integrating AI and expanding its product ecosystem.

sources.summary: In 2024, Atlassian launched Rovo and acquired Rewatch; in 2025, they acquired Cycle App Inc. and The Browser Company.
Atlassian announced a new $1.5 billion share repurchase program and highlighted AI advancements in FY25.
Atlassian reported over $5.2 billion in revenue for FY25, with strong AI integration driving growth.
Atlassian Partner of the Year Awards 2024-2025 recognized innovative products and services from partners.
Atlassian is a global software company focused on unleashing team potential with AI-powered collaboration tools.

key_threats: Atlassian's Enterprise plan offers advanced features like BYOK encryption and centralized administration, which Figma cannot match for large organizations.
Atlassian Intelligence integrates AI to automate repetitive tasks, providing a productivity boost that Figma lacks.
The deep penetration of Atlassian in the enterprise market makes it difficult for Figma to compete for large-scale deployments.
Atlassian's strong AI capabilities and partnerships, such as with Google Cloud, enhance their cloud transformation, posing a challenge to Figma's growth.
Atlassian's cross-selling strategy, where 90% of customers use more than 3 products, creates a strong ecosystem that Figma struggles to break into.
opportunities: Atlassian lacks a strong focus on design-specific tools, which Figma can exploit by enhancing its design collaboration features.
Atlassian's products are heavily enterprise-focused, leaving a gap for Figma to target smaller teams with more agile and flexible solutions.
Figma can capitalize on Atlassian's limited social and collaborative features by expanding its own social design tools.
Atlassian's complex pricing structure can be a pain point for users, allowing Figma to offer simpler, more transparent pricing models.
Figma can leverage its web-based platform to offer seamless cross-platform collaboration, a feature that Atlassian's desktop-heavy tools may lack.

competitors.name: Balsamiq

pricing.content: Balsamiq offers several pricing plans tailored to different user needs. The Starter plan costs $16 per month per editor, billed annually at $192. The Teams plan is priced at $35 per month per editor, billed annually at $420, and includes features like up to 400 projects and 2,500 monthly AI credits per editor. Balsamiq also offers a free 14-day trial for new users, allowing them to explore the platform without any initial cost.

sources.summary: Balsamiq's Starter plan is $16/month/editor, billed annually at $192. The Teams plan is $35/month/editor, billed annually at $420, with features like up to 400 projects and 2,500 monthly AI credits per editor.
Major version updates for Balsamiq Desktop are priced at 50% of a new license, with a 1-user update costing $74.50.
Balsamiq's SCIM provisioning is gated behind premium plans, with SAML SSO integration available on Enterprise plans at $599/month.

key_features.content: Balsamiq is known for its low-fidelity wireframing capabilities, which include features like drag-and-drop wireframing, real-time collaboration, and the ability to add annotations and comments. The platform supports creating interactive prototypes by linking wireframes, and it offers a Quick Add feature for rapid UI control addition. Balsamiq also provides educational resources through The Wireframe Academy, which includes articles, videos, and courses on wireframing and UI/UX design.

sources.summary: Balsamiq allows for markup, real-time collaboration, and includes The Wireframe Academy for learning wireframing and UI/UX design.
Balsamiq features interactive prototypes, Quick Add for UI controls, and supports creating click-through prototypes.
Balsamiq Cloud offers rapid wireframing with features like drag-and-drop, search, and Quick Draw for creating wireframes.

market_positioning.content: Balsamiq positions itself as a tool for product builders rather than designers, focusing on early-stage wireframing and idea validation. It is designed to be simple and approachable, making it ideal for teams that need to quickly iterate on ideas without the complexity of high-fidelity design tools. Balsamiq emphasizes its utility in structuring and aligning team efforts before moving to more detailed design phases, often suggesting a workflow that starts with Balsamiq and transitions to tools like Figma for visual polish.

sources.summary: Balsamiq is built for product builders, focusing on early-stage wireframing, while Figma is for high-fidelity UI design.
Balsamiq is better for early-stage wireframing and working with non-designers, while Figma excels in high-fidelity UI work.
Balsamiq is not suited for mid or high-fidelity work but excels in low-fidelity wireframing, making it ideal for beginners.

target_audience.content: Balsamiq primarily targets product teams and designers who need to create low-fidelity wireframes quickly. It is particularly useful for teams that require speed and clarity in the early stages of product development. Balsamiq's tools are designed to help users focus on structure and flow rather than detailed design, making it a preferred choice for those who need to validate ideas and collaborate with non-designers. The platform is also favored by educators and beginners due to its simplicity and educational resources.

sources.summary: Product teams use Balsamiq for low-fidelity wireframes to make better product decisions with speed and clarity.
Balsamiq is favored for initial, low-fidelity UI designs, appealing to users who prefer simplicity over complex design tools.
Balsamiq offers tutorials and courses for beginners, focusing on rapid wireframing and user flow mapping.

recent_developments.content: In 2024, Balsamiq launched a new brand and website, along with a UI update for its wireframing tool, focusing on speed and clarity. The company has shifted its focus towards Balsamiq Cloud, with plans to discontinue sales of its Desktop version by December 31, 2026. Recent updates include improved snapping and alignment, simplified symbol editing, and a new sketch style. Balsamiq has also introduced a 10-project plan for growing teams and enhanced performance to reduce technical debt.

sources.summary: Balsamiq launched a new brand and UI update in 2024, focusing on speed and clarity for product teams.
Sales of Balsamiq for Desktop will stop on December 31, 2026, as the company focuses on Balsamiq Cloud.
Recent updates include improved snapping, alignment, and a new sketch style, with a focus on Balsamiq Cloud.

key_threats: Balsamiq's low pricing for entry-level plans ($16/month/editor) makes it accessible for small teams, challenging Figma's higher pricing tiers.
The platform's focus on rapid, low-fidelity wireframing allows teams to quickly iterate and validate ideas, potentially reducing the need for more complex tools like Figma.
Balsamiq's educational resources, such as The Wireframe Academy, attract beginners and educators, building a loyal user base early in their design journey.
opportunities: Balsamiq lacks mid and high-fidelity design capabilities; Figma can capitalize by enhancing its low-fidelity features to attract Balsamiq users.
The absence of advanced prototyping features in Balsamiq presents an opportunity for Figma to emphasize its robust prototyping tools.
Balsamiq's limited diagramming and whiteboarding capabilities can be exploited by Figma by promoting its comprehensive design and collaboration features.

competitors.name: Banani

pricing.content: Banani offers a tiered pricing model with a free plan and three paid tiers. The Plus plan costs $20/month or $12/month when billed annually, while the Pro plan is priced at $50/month or $30/month annually. An Enterprise plan is available with custom pricing. All paid plans offer a 40% discount when billed annually, and include features like unlimited Figma exports and code exports.

sources.summary: Banani pricing has three tiers: Plus at $20/month or $12/month annually, Pro at $50/month or $30/month annually, and a free plan. Enterprise pricing is custom.
Banani's Plus plan is $20/month or $12/month annually, Pro is $50/month or $30/month annually, with a free plan and custom Enterprise pricing.
Banani AI offers a free plan with 20 screen generations per month, Plus plan at $12/month for 100 generations, and Pro at $30/month for unlimited generations.

key_features.content: Banani's key features include text-to-prototype capabilities, allowing users to generate multi-screen UI designs from text prompts. It supports natural language edits, enabling users to modify layouts, colors, and components through chat. Banani also offers Figma and code exports, making it easy to integrate designs into existing workflows. The platform is designed for rapid UI prototyping, catering to product teams that need to move quickly from idea to interface.

sources.summary: Banani's flagship feature is text-to-prototype, generating editable, multi-screen UI from prompts.
Banani AI allows users to describe ideas in plain language to generate multi-screen designs, editable by chat, and exportable to Figma or code.
Banani AI generates complete UI screens, wireframes, and design flows using text prompts, blending automation with manual control.

market_positioning.content: Banani positions itself as an AI-driven design tool that simplifies the UI design process for product teams. It emphasizes speed and ease of use, allowing users to generate and edit designs without needing extensive design experience. Banani is particularly appealing to non-designers and product managers who need to quickly visualize and iterate on prototypes. Its integration with Figma and code export capabilities further enhance its appeal to teams looking for seamless workflow integration.

sources.summary: Banani is positioned as an AI design tool that simplifies UI design for product teams, emphasizing speed and ease of use.
Banani is suited for product managers, founders, and non-designers needing rapid UI prototyping, with features like Figma export and real-time collaboration.
Banani AI is a productivity tool for designers, offering speed and control in generating UI designs from text prompts.

target_audience.content: Banani targets product teams, founders, and non-designers who need to quickly move from idea to interface without waiting on a designer. It is ideal for generating UI designs, UX flows, and app UIs, making it suitable for web apps, mobile apps, and SaaS dashboards. Banani's ease of use and rapid prototyping capabilities make it a valuable tool for teams that require fast iterations and seamless integration with tools like Figma.

sources.summary: Banani is built for product teams needing to move from idea to interface quickly, supporting mobile and desktop UI design.
Banani generates multi-screen, interactive prototypes for web apps, mobile apps, and SaaS dashboards, with Figma export capabilities.

recent_developments.content: In May 2025, Banani raised €850,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by Specialist VC and Inovo VC. The funding will be used to enhance its AI design tool, improve user flow prediction, and expand collaboration features. Established in 2024, Banani aims to become a central product-design hub for teams by building advanced layers connecting user insights.

sources.summary: Banani raised €850,000 in May 2025 to enhance its AI design tool and expand collaboration features.
Banani secured €850,000 in pre-seed funding in May 2025, led by Specialist VC and Inovo VC, to enhance its AI design tool.

key_threats: Banani offers a free plan with monthly credit refills, making it attractive to budget-conscious users who might otherwise choose Figma.
Its text-to-prototype feature allows rapid UI generation, potentially reducing the need for traditional design tools like Figma.
Banani's integration with Figma for seamless design export could attract Figma users looking for enhanced AI capabilities.
The ability to edit designs using natural language could appeal to non-designers, expanding Banani's user base beyond traditional designers.
opportunities: Banani lacks advanced collaborative features found in Figma; enhancing real-time collaboration could attract more team-based users.
Its design outputs may not be as polished as Figma's; improving design quality could help capture more professional designers.
Banani's focus on rapid prototyping leaves room for Figma to emphasize its comprehensive design system capabilities.
The absence of a strong community and resource base like Figma's presents an opportunity for Figma to leverage its existing ecosystem.

recommended_actions.action: Enhance AI capabilities in Figma to match or exceed competitors like Adobe and Banani.
recommended_actions.rationale: AI is a significant differentiator in the design software market, and enhancing these capabilities could significantly improve Figma's competitive position.

recommended_actions.action: Develop a mobile app to expand Figma's accessibility and usability on mobile devices.
recommended_actions.rationale: A mobile app would enhance Figma's appeal to users who need to work on the go, aligning with competitors like Adobe and Atlassian.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce more flexible pricing plans to attract a broader range of users, including small teams and freelancers.
recommended_actions.rationale: Flexible pricing can attract a wider audience and compete more effectively with the diverse pricing strategies of competitors.

recommended_actions.action: Strengthen collaboration features to maintain Figma's edge over competitors like Balsamiq and Banani.
recommended_actions.rationale: Collaboration is a core strength of Figma, and enhancing these features can help retain and grow its user base.

recommended_actions.action: Expand enterprise solutions to better compete with Atlassian's strong presence in the enterprise market.
recommended_actions.rationale: Enterprise solutions are crucial for capturing large organizational clients, which are a significant revenue source.
